prompt: The candidate runs on the integration rig. A service instruction for one supported language still points to the old diagnostic, although its file passed the publication checks. What should the release lead record?

options.text: Mark the software build ready and record the whole product as releasable on the same date.
options.feedback: The build record can support the software claim. A technician using that language would still receive the wrong service instruction.

options.text: Hold the whole release until the corrected edition is reviewed, packaged and checked against this candidate.
options.feedback: The translation is part of the agreed release. Testing the link from the candidate and reviewing the wording establish that the technician can reach the right instruction and interpret it.

options.text: Accept the current edition and use the deployment window as the deadline for its review.
options.feedback: This would move required work past the point at which the team claimed readiness. Operations needs a complete package before it chooses a deployment window.

prompt: During the diagnostic review someone asks to change the message from “Indication unknown” to “Amber confirmed” whenever the adapter returns a receipt. How should the coordinator handle the request?

options.text: Use the expedited wording review because the event code and screen location stay the same.
options.feedback: The new words make a different claim about the lamp. A review of the wording cannot establish that the indicated color was observed.

options.text: Run the peak-load check and accept the new meaning if every receipt arrives before the response limit.
options.feedback: A timely receipt establishes when a message arrived. It leaves the lamp state undetermined for that head and command.

options.text: Refer the new claim to the interface owner and require evidence of the displayed indication before authorizing it.
options.feedback: The change crosses the agreed boundary for a diagnostic wording update. The responsible owner must resolve the contract and the reviewer needs independent evidence tied to the configuration.

prompt: The service-language review repeatedly starts after the software is ready. Which investment would directly address that wait on the next change?

options.text: Route changes to each affected language reviewer at request acceptance and flag editions tied to old wording.
options.feedback: Review can begin during implementation, and a version check can expose outstanding editions before the release decision. Each reviewer still judges meaning in context.

options.text: Add agent capacity to the controller build and measure time from compilation to the first successful software check.
options.feedback: The software already finishes first. This measure stops before the service review that determines whole-product readiness.

options.text: Reuse the previous release’s language approvals whenever the diagnostic code stays the same.
options.feedback: A stable identifier helps locate the right reviewer. An approval belongs to the wording and product revision that person actually reviewed.
